position_in_era.primary_genre_lineage: flamenco × Catalan-folk × fado × Cuban × song-form translation
position_in_era.historical_role: The Catalan-rooted vocalist who sustains the *song-form* translation across folk, acoustic jazz, fado, flamenco, Cuban, Brazilian — sometimes within a single album, frequently across four languages (Catalan, Spanish, Portuguese, Galician). *11 de Novembre* (2012) is her first proper solo album of original songs. A defining female-translation voice of the 2010s, methodologically descending from Buika and from the Lebrijano-orchestral lineage in the same way Dorantes does.

narrative_slots.production_facts: Released 2012. Pérez Cruz composed and arranged all material; co-produced with Raül Fernández Refree. Album titled after her late father Cástor Pérez's birthday.
narrative_slots.member_dynamics: Father (musician Cástor Pérez) died two days before his birthday; album becomes a memorial dedication.
narrative_slots.cultural_venue: Palafrugell, Catalonia (havaneras tradition); Barcelona contemporary scene.
narrative_slots.instrumentation_details: Voice plus acoustic chamber arrangements drawing from flamenco, fado, jazz, Catalan-folk; multilingual.
narrative_slots.release_circumstances: Gold-certified in Spain (20,000+ copies — significant for an independent release).
